release.name: CNA C ABI 0.1.0, experimental
release.note: This gate governs publishing an **experimental** C ABI release. ABI 1.0 -- the point at which only additive changes are permitted within a major version -- is a separate decision that this gate does not make and must not be read as making.

criteria.title: The compatibility matrix is real, current and honest
criteria.requirement: Every public header compiles on its own, in every declared language mode of every installed toolchain, and the published matrix matches its declaration.
criteria.evidence: docs/c-api/COMPATIBILITY.md, gated by CApiCompatibilityMatrix and CApiHeaderCompatibility
criteria.note: C99 is a verified floor rather than a claim: the matrix found and killed a duplicate typedef that made C99 impossible.

criteria.title: No unreviewed ABI break
criteria.requirement: Every struct layout, field offset, scalar width, constant value and exported symbol is recorded, and a change to any of them arrives as a reviewable diff.
criteria.evidence: tools/c-api/abi_baseline.json, gated by CApiAbiHeaderBaseline and CApiAbiBaseline
criteria.note: The header half needs no build and runs everywhere; the export half runs in each C API build tree.

criteria.title: No public C++ symbol is unaccounted for
criteria.requirement: The generated inventory has no `planned` row: every public declaration is mapped, partially mapped with its subset named, or recorded as having no C form with the reason.
criteria.note: Closing the remaining partial rows is CBIND-044 and is not a condition of an experimental release.

criteria.title: A known-limitations matrix a reader can act on
criteria.requirement: What the ABI does not do is published, grouped by reason, with no unclassified reason and no deferral owned by a finished task.
criteria.note: This is the document a consumer reads to decide whether to adopt the ABI at all.

criteria.title: A real C application, built the way a consumer builds one
criteria.requirement: A complete C program exists, is built from outside the source tree against an installed CNA through find_package, and is run.
criteria.note: A program that only builds inside this repository would prove nothing about the package.

criteria.title: The package is installable and findable
criteria.requirement: `find_package(CNA CONFIG)` resolves from an installed prefix and yields one target, and the package version is the C ABI version.
criteria.evidence: modules/c-api/cmake/CNAConfig.cmake.in and the CNACApi install component
criteria.note: Before CBIND-041 the module installed a targets file and no package config, so this criterion was silently false.

criteria.title: The consumer documentation exists
criteria.requirement: Consumption, handles, errors, strings and buffers, callbacks and threading, renderer capabilities, ABI versioning and fuzzing are each documented.
criteria.note: CONSUMING.md is the entry point for somebody who has never read this repository.

criteria.title: The lifetime and byte-facing contracts are measured, not asserted
criteria.requirement: Handle lifetime, teardown ordering and buffer boundaries are stressed under a sanitizer, and the surfaces that read caller-supplied bytes are covered against an independent oracle.
criteria.note: The stress suite found a heap use-after-free on its first run; that is what this criterion is for.

criteria.title: Whether the package ships its native dependencies
criteria.requirement: A decision on whether SDL3, SDL3_image, SDL3_mixer and FFmpeg are installed alongside libcna_c_api.so, or whether placing them is the consumer's job.
criteria.check: owner_decision_still_open:The package does not ship SDL3 or FFmpeg
criteria.evidence: docs/c-api/LIMITATIONS.md, recorded as an open decision
criteria.note: Not a defect and not something an implementer may settle: it is a redistribution decision. Until it is ruled on, a consumer must place those libraries themselves, and this gate reports the release as not ready.

criteria.title: Whether a static configuration is ever offered
criteria.requirement: A decision on `CNA_C_API_STATIC`, which names a configuration that does not exist.
criteria.evidence: docs/c-api/LIMITATIONS.md, recorded as an open decision
criteria.note: A static build would export every C++ symbol it archived, and the ABI promise -- 2,720 cna_* names and nothing else -- would stop meaning anything. Offering one requires a design, not a build option.
